title: Cyclic branched covers and knot determinants

items.title: Finiteness and order of the cokernel of a square integer matrix
items.statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix with integer entries. Define $\operatorname{coker}(A)=\mathbb Z^n/A\mathbb Z^n$. Then $\operatorname{coker}(A)$ is finite if and only if $\det A\ne0$, and in that case its order is $|\det A|$. For the empty $0\times0$ matrix, take $\det A=1$ and $\operatorname{coker}(A)=0$.
items.strategy: Reduce by unimodular integer row and column operations to a diagonal matrix and compute its cokernel.

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links
references.locator: Chapter 8.B, printed pp. 204–206; integer row/column operations and square presentation order ideal generated by the determinant

items.title: Inverse-matrix formula for a surgery linking form
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $J=J_1\cup\cdots\cup J_n$ be an oriented link of $n\ge1$ smooth components in $S^3$. Choose pairwise disjoint closed tubular neighborhoods $N(J_i)$, let $X=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}(\bigcup_iN(J_i))$, and let $\mu_i$ be the positive meridian of $J_i$. Let $\lambda_i$ be the longitude parallel to $J_i$ with zero self-linking. Alexander duality identifies $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ with $\mathbb Z^n$ on the meridian basis $[\mu_1],\ldots,[\mu_n]$; for $i\ne j$, define $\operatorname{lk}_{S^3}(J_i,J_j)$ to be the $j$-th coordinate of $[\lambda_i]$, the usual oriented linking number. Use the boundary-torus intersection convention $\mu_i\mathbin{\cdot}\lambda_i=+1$. Give $J_i$ an integer framing $f_i$ and fill along $\delta_i=\lambda_i+f_i\mu_i$. Let $A$ be the symmetric integer matrix with $A_{ii}=f_i$ and $A_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}_{S^3}(J_i,J_j)$ for $i\ne j$. Assume $\det A\ne0$, and let $Y$ be the resulting oriented surgery manifold, oriented as the boundary of the 4-dimensional surgery handlebody with outward normal first. Then $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^n/A\mathbb Z^n$. For torsion classes $[C],[D]\in H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$ represented by oriented 1-cycles, choose $m>0$ and an integral 2-chain $F$ with $\partial F=mC$ and define $\lambda_Y([C],[D])=(F\mathbin{\cdot}D)/m\pmod{\mathbb Z}$, where the intersection is signed by the orientation of $Y$. If $x,y\in\mathbb Z^n$ are meridian-coordinate representatives of $[C],[D]$, then
$$
\lambda_Y([x],[y])=-x^TA^{-1}y\pmod{\mathbb Z}.
$$

references.title: Jozef H. Przytycki and Akira Yasuhara, Linking Numbers in Rational Homology 3-Spheres, Cyclic Branched Covers and Infinite Cyclic Covers
references.locator: Section 1, printed pp. 4–7, Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2; surgery comparison and reverse-link matrix

items.strategy: Use Mayer–Vietoris for the surgery presentation and compare linking before and after filling by the rational inverse of the framed-link matrix.

items.title: Cyclic branched cover of a knot
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, choose its compact exterior $E_K$ with boundary torus $T_K$, and let $\mu$ and $\lambda$ be its positive meridian and preferred longitude. The exterior homology theorem gives $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu]$. Let $\phi:\pi_1(E_K)\to\mathbb Z$ be the composite of abelianization with the homomorphism $[\mu]\mapsto1$. For an integer $q\ge2$, let $\phi_q$ be the composite $\pi_1(E_K)\xrightarrow{\phi}\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$, and let $p_q:E_q\to E_K$ be the connected cover classified by $\ker\phi_q$. On $T_K$, the homomorphism sends $[\mu]\mapsto1$ and $[\lambda]\mapsto0$, so the preimage of $T_K$ is a connected torus cover whose fundamental group corresponds to $\langle\mu^q,\lambda\rangle$. Let $\widetilde\mu$ be the closed lift of $\mu^q$. Attach a solid torus to $E_q$ with its meridian identified with $\widetilde\mu$; the resulting oriented closed $3$-manifold is the $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $\Sigma_q(K)$. In tubular coordinates near $K$, the extended map to $S^3$ has local form $(s,w)\mapsto(s,w^q)$, and the deck group $\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$ acts by $w\mapsto e^{2\pi i/q}w$.

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links
references.locator: Chapter 10.C, printed pp. 297–300

items.strategy: Define the exterior cover by the meridian homomorphism and fill its lifted meridian.

items.title: Homology of a cyclic branched cover as Alexander-module coinvariants
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $X_K=S^3\setminus K$, and let $q\ge2$. Let $A_K=H_1(\widetilde X_K;\mathbb Z)$ be the one-variable Alexander module with the positive-meridian deck action $t$. Then, as abelian groups,
$$
H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\cong A_K/(t^q-1)A_K.
$$

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links
references.locator: Chapter 10.C, printed pp. 297–300; finite cyclic cover and filling construction

items.strategy: Abelianize the semidirect product of the infinite-cyclic subgroup by the q-th meridian and then kill the lifted meridian in the filling.

items.title: Surgery presentation from a Seifert surface
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ bound a connected compact oriented Seifert surface $F$ of genus $g$. Choose a disk-band decomposition of $F$ with one disk and $2g$ bands, and use its band-core basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ to form the positive-push Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. For $q\ge2$, define the symmetric block matrix $M_q(V)$ of size $2g(q-1)$ by specifying its $2g\times2g$ blocks, indexed by $1\le k,\ell\le q-1$:
$$(M_q(V))_{k\ell}=\begin{cases}V+V^T,&k=\ell,\\-V^T,&\ell=k+1,\\-V,&k=\ell+1,\\0,&|k-\ell|\ge2.\end{cases}$$
Push the interior of $F$ into $B^4$ while keeping $K$ on $S^3=\partial B^4$, cut $B^4$ along a thickened copy of the pushed-in surface, and take $q$ copies. For $i=1,\ldots,q-1$, glue the positive face of copy $i$ to the negative face of copy $i+1$ by reflecting the normal coordinate; do not glue the last positive face to the first negative face. Call the resulting $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $W_q(F)$. It has one $0$-handle and $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles, and its framed attaching link has linking matrix $M_q(V)$. The boundary branched cover, with the boundary marking induced by the covering map, is $\Sigma_q(K)$.

references.title: Selman Akbulut and Robion Kirby, Branched Covers of Surfaces in 4-Manifolds
references.locator: Section 2, printed pp. 113–117; cyclic branched cover of B^4 and band-handle construction

items.strategy: Use the q-copy branched-handle construction and compute each framed-link entry from the two Seifert push-offs.

items.title: Seifert block presentation of cyclic branched-cover homology
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a connected compact oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and choose any ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ with positive-push Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. For an integer $q\ge2$, let $M_q(V)$ be the symmetric block matrix of size $2g(q-1)$ whose $2g\times2g$ block in position $(k,\ell)$, for $1\le k,\ell\le q-1$, is $V+V^T$ if $k=\ell$, $-V^T$ if $\ell=k+1$, $-V$ if $k=\ell+1$, and $0$ if $|k-\ell|\ge2$. Then
$$
H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{coker}(M_q(V)).
$$
For $q=2$ this presentation matrix is $V+V^T$; when $g=0$ the empty matrix has trivial cokernel.

items.title: Homology of the double branched cover from a Seifert matrix
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a connected compact oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $V$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix in any ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Then
$$
H_1(\Sigma_2(K);\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{coker}(V+V^T).
$$
For $g=0$, the matrix is empty and the cokernel is trivial.

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links
references.locator: Chapter 8.D, printed pp. 212–213; proof of the double-cover presentation

items.title: Root-product test for cyclic branched-cover homology
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a connected compact oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $V$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix in an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Write $\Delta_K(t)$ for the Alexander polynomial normalized up to multiplication by $\pm t^k$, and let $q\ge2$ with $\zeta_q$ a primitive $q$-th root of unity. Then $H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)$ is finite if and only if $\Delta_K(\zeta_q^j)\ne0$ for every $1\le j<q$, and, when it is finite,
$$
|H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)|=\prod_{j=1}^{q-1}|\Delta_K(\zeta_q^j)|.
$$
The same criterion and order hold when $\Delta_K(t)$ is replaced by $\det(V-tV^T)$.

items.title: Knot determinant is the order of double-cover homology
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K(t)$ normalized up to multiplication by $\pm t^k$. Then $H_1(\Sigma_2(K);\mathbb Z)$ is finite if and only if $\Delta_K(-1)\ne0$, and in that case
$$
|H_1(\Sigma_2(K);\mathbb Z)|=|\Delta_K(-1)|.
$$
Moreover, $\Delta_K(-1)$ is odd, so the first homology of every double branched cover is finite.

items.title: Cyclic-cover homology order from the Alexander polynomial
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $q\ge2$. If $\zeta_q$ is any primitive $q$-th root of unity, then $H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)$ is finite exactly when $\Delta_K(\zeta_q^j)\ne0$ for every $1\le j<q$, and in that case
$$
|H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)|=\prod_{j=1}^{q-1}|\Delta_K(\zeta_q^j)|.
$$

title: Cyclic branched covers and knot determinants — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Worked cases: double branched covers of the trefoil, figure-eight knot, and unknot
items.statement:
For the right-handed trefoil and figure-eight knot, use their standard genus-one Seifert surfaces and the ordered bases whose positive-push Seifert matrices are, respectively,
$$V_T=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V_8=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Their double branched covers have first homology $\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z$ and $\mathbb Z/5\mathbb Z$, respectively. The double branched cover of the unknot is $S^3$.
